en.title: Bluey Makers' Alien Comedy 'Allen' Lands November 2026 on Netflix
en.summary: Get ready for an out-of-this-world family movie night. The Australian studio behind the beloved animated series 'Bluey' is bringing a new live-action sci-fi comedy to Netflix next year.
en.body:
Prepare for a cosmic reunion that’s two decades in the making. Netflix has officially announced that **Allen**, the new live-action sci-fi family comedy from Australia’s acclaimed **Ludo Studio** (the creative minds behind the global phenomenon **Bluey**), will premiere worldwide on **Thursday, November 12th, 2026**. This marks a significant move for Ludo Studio into live-action feature films, following their massive success in animation.

The film promises a unique blend of humor and heart, centered around Petey, a man who has never quite moved on from a childhood encounter with an alien. Now, 20 years later, his extraterrestrial friend has crash-landed back into his life, bringing with it a complicated and unexpected reason for their reunion. The concept echoes the nostalgic, heartwarming feel of classics like **E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial**, but with a distinctly adult perspective on lingering childhood connections.

Creator and co-director **Daley Pearson** shared his vision for the project, stating, "Allen is really a story about love, family and all those big and small moments from childhood that end up shaping who we are when we grow up. Getting the opportunity to make this story in this part of the world – in the town where I grew up in, inspired by the friends and family I grew up with – is a dream. We're creating Allen for families to watch together."

## A Nostalgic Return to the Stars

This announcement is a delightful surprise for fans who have been captivated by Ludo Studio's masterful storytelling. While **Bluey** has charmed audiences with its relatable family dynamics and gentle humor, **Allen** suggests a venture into more fantastical territory, albeit with the same focus on emotional resonance. The premise of an adult revisiting a childhood alien encounter offers fertile ground for exploring themes of lost innocence, the passage of time, and the enduring power of extraordinary friendships. It’s a concept that appeals directly to the binge-watching generation who grew up with their own formative sci-fi experiences and now appreciate narratives that blend nostalgia with mature storytelling.

Netflix's VP of Content for APAC, **Minyoung Kim**, expressed her enthusiasm, noting that Ludo Studio are "among Australia's most exceptional storytellers" and that the streamer is "delighted to create a film that the entire family can enjoy." The anticipation for this film is palpable, especially given the studio's proven track record for creating content that resonates deeply with audiences worldwide.

## What Fans Are Saying

The buzz surrounding **Allen** is already significant, fueled by the pedigree of its creators. Fans are eager to see how Ludo Studio translates its unique brand of storytelling into a live-action sci-fi comedy. The comparison to **E.T.**, a film that holds a special place in the hearts of many, has only amplified expectations. Viewers are speculating about the tone of the film, wondering if it will lean more into quirky comedy or heartfelt drama, or perhaps a perfect balance of both. The specific release date, November 12th, 2026, gives audiences ample time to prepare for what promises to be a memorable cinematic event.

## What's Next

Mark your calendars for **November 12th, 2026**, when **Allen** premieres globally on Netflix. In the meantime, fans can revisit the heartwarming world of **Bluey** or keep an eye out for further announcements regarding the cast and any additional sneak peeks from Ludo Studio and Netflix.

content_raw: Picture Credit: Netflix Netflix has revealed that Allen , the new live-action family film from Ludo Studio, the Emmy and BAFTA-winning Australian studio behind Bluey , will land globally on Netflix on Thursday, November 12th, 2026. Alongside the date, Netflix released a short but very funny teaser that’s sure to catch a few people out. Here’s everything you need to know about  Allen a month before its release, noting that you can find our previous coverage of the movie here and Netflix’s upcoming Aussie and Kiwi slate here .  What is Allen about? Allen is an Australian sci-fi family comedy about a man who never quite got over his childhood alien encounter. Netflix’s official logline reads: 20 years after his encounter with an alien, Petey never moved on. Now his old friend has returned, and the reason why is complicated — and unexpected. Think E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial , but picking up two decades later, when the kid has grown up and his extraterrestrial best friend comes crash-landing back into his life. Creator and co-director Daley Pearson said of the project when it entered production: “Allen is really a story about love, family and all those big and small moments from childhood that end up shaping who we are when we grow up. Getting the opportunity to make this story in this part of the world – in the town where I grew up in, inspired by the friends and family I grew up with – is a dream. We’re creating Allen for families to watch together.” Netflix’s VP of Content for APAC, Minyoung Kim, added that Ludo Studio are “among Australia’s most exceptional storytellers” and that the streamer is “delighted to create a film that the entire family can enjoy.” Watch the teaser for Allen Netflix’s 26-second teaser for Allen is a brilliant bait-and-switch. It opens with a slow, ominous pan over Earth from space, with fragmented glowing lines gradually assembling into a title. If you’re getting flashbacks to Ridley Scott’s 1979 classic Alien , that’s entirely the point, as the letters look set to spell out A L I E N before shuffling into the far more mundane A L L E N. From there, a pulsing purple spacecraft descends onto a misty field at night. Petey watches on as the door slides open to reveal a gangly silhouette, before a robotic voice announces: “Allen came back!” Petey’s response? A wide-eyed scream that’s somewhere between pure joy and total panic. It’s certainly an interesting way to introduce the film, and judging by the comments, more than a few people clicked expecting a new Alien project before realizing what they’d stumbled into. Who is cast in Allen ? T.J. Power ( Offspring ) leads the cast as the grown-up Petey.
